steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This place? Why, this is Rellekka! Homeland of all Fremennik! I do not recognise your face outerlander; Where do you come from?

steps.player: That's not important...

steps.npc: Hmmm... I will not press the issue then outerlander. How may my tribe and I help you?

steps.player: Do you have any quests?

steps.npc: Quests, you say outerlander? Well, I would not call it a quest as such, but if you are brave of heart and strong of body, perhaps...
No, you would not be interested. Forget I said anything, outerlander.

steps.player: Actually, I would be very interested to hear what you have to offer.

steps.npc: You would? These are unusual sentiments to hear from an outerlander! My suggestion was going to be that if you crave adventure and battle,
and your heart sings for glory, then perhaps you would be interested in joining our clan, and becoming a Fremennik yourself?

steps.player: What would that involve exactly?

steps.npc: Well, there are two ways to become a member of our clan and call yourself a Fremennik: be born a Fremennik, or be voted in by our council of elders.

steps.player: Well, I think I've missed the first way, but how can I get the council of elders to vote to let me join your clan?

steps.npc: Well, that I cannot answer myself. You will need to speak to each of them and see what they require of you as proof of your dedication.
There are twelve council members around this village; you will need to gain a majority vote of at least seven councillors in your favour.
So what say you? Give me the word, and I will tell all of my tribe of your intentions, be they yea or nay.

steps.player: You're right. I really couldn't care less.

steps.npc: It is as I thought outerlander. Your kind care nothing for the Fremennik, and we feel the same about you. This is the way of the world.

options.text: Why will no-one talk to me?

steps.player: Why will no-one talk to me?

steps.npc: Do not take it personally, outerlander! We are a simple people, and it is our experience that keeping ourselves to ourselves is best. This is why speaking to outerlanders is forbidden.
We do not wish to enter war with the outerlanders and their strange magics, so we limit all unauthorised communication.

steps.player: Then how come you're talking to me?

steps.npc: Ah, this is because I am the chieftain. I am the one who authorises contact. You will not find many of my tribe so forthcoming with you, as I.

steps.player: Is there a way for you to authorise your tribe to talk to me then?

steps.npc: Well, there is one way... but I doubt it is of any interest to you.

steps.player: Actually, I would be very interested to hear what you have to offer.

steps.npc: You would? These are unusual sentiments to hear from an outerlander! My suggestion was going to be that if you crave adventure and battle,
and your heart sings for glory, then perhaps you would be interested in joining our clan, and becoming a Fremennik yourself?

steps.player: What would that involve exactly?

steps.npc: Well, there are two ways to become a member of our clan and call yourself a Fremennik: be born a Fremennik, or be voted in by our council of elders.

So what say you? Give me the word, and I will tell all of my tribe of your intentions, be they yea or nay.

options.text: Why do you call me outerlander?

steps.player: Why do you call me outerlander?

steps.npc: Do not take it as an insult, outerlander. For us, this town is the center of all. Anyone not born here, or that we do not know and trust is an outerlander.

steps.player: So it basically means stranger?

steps.npc: Aye, but that is an outerlander word. We do not judge someones ways by their name. It simply means one from the outerlands, or one not from Rellekka.
I know our customs are foreign to you; perhaps you would like me to explain something else?

options.text: I seek an army to destroy Asgarnia!

steps.player: I seek an army to destroy Asgarnia!

steps.npc: We will have no part in the squabbles of outerlander tribes. Their magics are strange and deadly to us, as we learnt long ago.
If this is all that you came here for, then you have had a wasted journey. If you are looking for something else, then speak now for my patience dwindles.

steps.player: Who are the Fremennik?

steps.npc: It is the name we call ourselves. Outerlanders tend to call us 'Barbarian', but they do not understand our ways...

options.text: Why will no-one talk to me?

steps.player: Nice hat!

steps.npc: Do not mock me outerlander; this helm has saved my life more times than I care to recall right now.

options.text: Ask about a Seal of Passage

steps.player: Do you have any quests?

steps.speaker: Brundt
steps.text: As a matter of fact [Fremennik name], I do have a quest for you. Are you interested?

steps.player: I'm ready for adventure

steps.speaker: Brundt
steps.text: Excellent, now-

steps.player: So what will it be this time? Joining warring islands?

steps.speaker: Brundt
steps.text: I'm a fan of you enthusiasm, [Fremennik name], but-

steps.player: Would you have me slay a mighty daggermouth? Or do you need my expertise in conquering untamed lands?

steps.speaker: Brundt
steps.text: Nothing quite that fancy I'm afraid, [Fremennik name]. I just need you to investigate a minor disturbance.

steps.player: Oh.

steps.speaker: Brundt
steps.text: Freygerd and Reeso run the sandpit a little north of here. They mentioned they heard some rustling by their hut lat night and wanted an official to investigate. You've proven yourself more than worthy of our people's trust.

steps.player: Well that doesn't sound so bad. I'll get right on it.

steps.speaker: Brundt
steps.text: Thank you, [Fremennik name].

steps.player: Not right now.

steps.speaker: Brundt
steps.text: Very well. Return when you wish to help.

steps.player: Hi there Brundt the Chieftain. Could you help me out with a Seal of Passage?

steps.npc: A Seal of Passage? Whatever for?

steps.player: Well, I've heard that there have been great troubles between your people and that of the Moon Clan. I was hoping to help. And so I need the Seal of Passage to show my intentions.

steps.npc: Ah [Fremennik name], many have tried, but The Moon Clan are by no means a sharing group of people. They do everything by magic, something we never use. But they are so secretive about it. If only they would share, we
wouldn't have to kill them all the time!

steps.player: I will see what I can do.
Can I have that seal then?

steps.npc: If you are to bring peace to our two warring clans, then perhaps it is best that you do...

steps.text: a seal of passage

steps.npc: Yes?

steps.player: I lost my Seal of Passage!

steps.npc: Then you had better take a replacement and be less careless in future.

steps.player: Already? News really does travel fast!

steps.npc: Thank you so very much, I think we can really make progress now.

steps.player: No worries. I am pleased I could help.
Oh, erm, could you help me out with a Seal of Passage?

steps.npc: Seal of Passage, well I suppose so.
Ok, here you go.

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.player: So how did the meeting go?

steps.npc: It went surprisingly well! We are at least at the point where we will freely acknowledge each other's existence now.
You are definitely a great asset to the Fremennik, [Fremennik name]!

steps.player: I've lost V's Shield.

steps.text: If the player still has V's shield:

steps.npc: I don't think you have [Fremennik name]. I suggest you try looking for it again.

steps.text: If the player has lost V's shield:

steps.npc: You really should be more careful [Fremennik name]. Luckily for you I found it again but you'll have to pay to get it back.

steps.player: How much?

steps.npc: 50,000 coins. Consider it a lesson in looking after things better.

steps.text: If the player has at least 50,000 coins:

steps.player: Sounds good to me.

steps.text: V's shield

steps.npc: Here you go [Fremennik name]. Use it well.

steps.player: That's a bit too much I'm afraid.

steps.npc: Fair enough. I'll be here if you change your mind.

steps.player: I don't have that much.

steps.npc: Well come back when you do.
Hello again [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]! I hope your travels have brought you wealth and joy! What compels you to visit me on this day?

options.text: I just came to say hello.

steps.player: I just came to say hello.

steps.npc: Well met, [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]. It is always good to see your face in glorious Rellekka once more!

steps.player: Do you have any quests?

steps.npc: Not at the moment [Fremennik name]. Rest assured, should your services to the Fremennik be required, I will call upon you.

steps.player: Nice hat!

steps.npc: Aye, that it is [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]. Should you desire one of your own, you should go to Skulgrimen's shop and see what they have available!

options.text: Can I hear the history of your people?

steps.player: Can I hear the history of your people?

steps.npc: Why, of course [Fremennik name]! Do not say 'your people' like that, for you are now a Fremennik yourself! What did you want to hear of?

options.text: Tell me of the finding of Koschei

steps.player: I'm interested in finding out about that mysterious warrior I fought as part of Thorvalds' combat trial. His name is Koschei I believe.

steps.npc: Ah... the deathless one... We do not even know if Koschei is his name, when we found him he had no memory, he was simply repeating that single word.
Whatever happened to him must have rattled his soul so hard that his memory ran away from him, and he has not yet found it's hiding place.

steps.player: So how exactly did you find him?

steps.npc: Well, it was a raiding party like any other. We had just struck one of the smaller northern islands to harvest supplies by combat, as our laws allow,
when we saw a figure in the icey waters. As we were at least a 3 week sail from any port, and saw no other ships nearby, he must have been there some time.
We could not leave someone to the cold death of the ocean, even an outerlander, so we fished him aboard. He muttered continually, but his words made no sense.
He had no clothes or possessions with him, and seemed to have been burnt somehow before he had landed in the water.
I cannot help but wonder what burnt him, for as you may have seen, he is incredibly powerful and resistant to damage by any means I know of!
Anyway, we decided to bring him back to Rellekka, for he did not seem of good health or sound mind, and simply repeated the word Koschei over and over.
Yrsa tended to him for many weeks, until one day it was as though a new soul had entered his burnt and broken body.
He suddenly left her house one day, fully healed, and able to speak to us as though nothing had happened to him.
He still had no recollection of how he had come to be in the icey ocean, or of who he was, or where he had come from, but this did not matter to us or him.
He took his trials of adulthood, as you did, and has been a boon to our clan ever since. Someday I fear he may regain his memory, and leave us for his past...
But I will always respect any decision he decides to make should that day ever come upon us. Until then, he is more than welcome to stay here.
So, [Fremennik name]. Was there anything more you wished to hear?

options.text: Tell me of the lands to the North

steps.player: I would like to hear of the lands across the ocean to the North.

steps.npc: Well, I think the best thing for you would be to go to the docks and ask to join one of our longboats on a journey.
My affairs are concentrated mostly on Rellekka, so my knowledge is not great, but I will happily share what I do know with you [Fremennik name].
North of this town the atmosphere becomes bitterly cold. There are a number of small inhabited islands that we have sea routes with.
The largest of these is possibly Miscellania, although I hear that there has been some recent incident with their monarch, but I don't know the details.
There is also of course the island of the moon clan, who change with the tides. They are our bitterest enemies, and we are currently at war with them.
They are an evil people, equally cursed and blessed by the magic in their blood. Beyond those islands, there is the large frozen wasteland we call Acheron.
It is an inhospitable land, and you will need an agile and sturdy body just to keep alive in it's perils.
As I say, my knowledge outside of this town is rather limited, and I know no more than this. Was there anything else you wished to hear tell of?

steps.player: I would like to hear a little of the history between the Fremenniks and the outerlanders.

steps.npc: Ah, now that is something I know a great deal about. Believe it or not, all outerlanders were once orginally Fremenniks.
When first man came to these lands all were Fremenniks, and followed our ways. We lived a happy life, and never settled in one place for long.
We travelled by boat along the coastlines, never taking more from the land than could be regrown by the same time in the following year.
However, many moons past, some of our tribesmen were weary of constantly travelling the lands, and decided to build themselves permanent homes.
Unfortunately, the other races that had also migrated here did not like this. They waged war against us at every opportunity.
We were driven mostly to the coastlines, where we could escape by boat when attacked. Remember, at this time we had no real way to defend against constant attack.
Then one day one of our Seers, whose name has been lost in the telling of this tale, discovered a cave full of strange rocks.
This rock would never be consumed, no matter how much we took, and sparkled at its peak, and broke off in small and regular sized chunks when mined.
Stranger than this, we found that these rocks would become filled with power when taken to certain places across this land!
There was a terrible argument in our tribe! Some said that we should take as many of these rocks as we could, and use them in defending against our enemies attacks!
Others said that we had found a place that belonged only to the gods, and that should we steal what was not ours we would find only torment and misery.
We voted on this, and decided that it was in the best interests of the tribe to leave these strange rocks where they lay, for the gods can be spiteful and cruel,
especially to those who do not treat them with the respect they desire. Some of our number refused to accept this ruling by our council however.
They began to mine these rocks, and set up transport systems to the various places of power that enchanted them.
They even created temples at each of these places! This was going too far! We had no choice, but to expel them from our tribe forever!
We turned our backs upon them, and let them know they would never be welcome back to our tribes until they had released themselves from the rocks.
This is the tale of how the outerlanders came about; through stealing from the gods, and from betraying our ideals. This is why we show them no trust.
Was there something else you wished to hear?

steps.player: Actually, history isn't really my thing.

steps.npc: Well let me know should you wish to hear our lore and histories. We value them highly.

steps.player: Nothing's wrong with [Fremennik name], I'd just like a new name, if it's not too much trouble.

steps.npc: Very well, from now on you will be known as [new Fremennik name] [honorific].
